items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: They had a Cuban drummer, the greatest of drummers. Can’t think of his name. Joe something.

ctx.x: On cruise ships. By that, he had worked, had all kinds of musicians he played with at different times. People would quit or they’d leave or you’d fire them, and you’d get the best you could on a ship. Did that for years. When I walked up, he was there waiting for me. I had to walk that whole hall at the Roosevelt, coming to the stand, and I got my banjo. Everybody looked at me like, scanning me, and I walked up and said, “Hello.” He said, “Hello. How are you? Welcome to the band. Come on in. Take your chances.…
Why did you first go to Chicago in 1921?
